title: Introduce stepwise RAG debug profiler quickstart
author: Anika Shah
release_notes: Add 'Stepwise RAG Debug Profiler' quickstart: instrument retrieval, model decision points, and tool calls for stepwise debugging.
New example runner in TypeScript and a Python harness for replayable traces.
Docs page added: docs/rag/debugging.md with troubleshooting and telemetry mapping.
body:
Context and motivation: This quickstart adds a compact developer-facing toolkit for tracing RAG flows at a stepwise granularity so engineers can inspect retrieval scores, model selection points, tool-call payloads, and KV-cache snapshots when debugging production regressions. Many teams at Redwood have asked for a small reproducible example that shows how to capture a deterministic decision trace, stream it to local telemetry, and replay a session in CI to catch regressions. The goal is a low-friction dev loop (local -> CI) that surfaces the most common causes of RAG failures (indexing drift, prompt-context truncation, tool binding errors, and KV-cache corruption) without adding heavy runtime overhead.

What this PR contains: A new quickstart under redwood-quickstarts/stepwise-rag-debug-profiler that includes: README.md with step-by-step setup and conceptual diagrams; example-runner.ts (TypeScript) — a small harness that runs a RAG session against a seeded compact index, records a stepwise trace (retriever scores, selected documents, prompt windows, model logits/decisions where available, tool inputs/outputs, KV-cache summaries), and writes a JSON trace to ./traces. A companion python/replay_harness.py that can replay traces deterministically in a CI job to assert stable outputs across model or infra changes. Minor docs change at docs/rag/debugging.md consolidates debugging tips and maps trace fields to Console telemetry dashboards. CI: adds ci/quickstarts-smoke.yml which runs the replay harness in a lightweight container to catch regressions on merge.

Highlights and rationale: - Stepwise trace format is intentionally compact: it records metadata per step (timestamp, step_type, retrieval_hint, top_k ids+scores, prompt_snapshot, model_response_summary, tools_called). This is designed to be readable and easy to filter in local tools or upload as an artifact in CI. - The TS runner uses the Redwood SDK to demonstrate a minimal instrumentation layer (hook points are small and copy-paste friendly). - The Python replay harness executes the same sequence with fixed random seeds and asserts that: retrieval ordering is stable, top-1 tool id is unchanged, and final answer includes an expected assertion snippet. This makes it practical for adding small smoke assertions to PRs that touch retrieval/model infra.

Backwards compatibility and safety: No runtime changes to the inference runtime or model serving. Quickstart is entirely opt-in — all code lives under redwood-quickstarts and examples. Sensitive fields are redacted in traces by default (PII masking in README). The trace format includes a small opt-out flag for customers who choose not to persist traces.

Testing and CI: Local unit tests for the trace serializer are included (tests/quickstarts/stepwise-profiler-smoke.test.ts), and the quickstart smoke workflow runs the replay harness on a pinned lightweight model. Initial CI run: lint caught formatting issues; those were fixed in the follow-up commit. E2E smoke required an additional retry due to a flaky network dependency; it passed on the second attempt. See CI checks summary for details.

Security and privacy: Traces default to redaction of full_text fields and contain hashes for document ids. README documents best practices for redaction and key management; the example harness shows how to stream traces to a local file or a secure telemetry sink (instructions for KMS-backed upload are linked).

Developer experience / Usage: 1) Clone repo and cd redwood-quickstarts/stepwise-rag-debug-profiler 2) npm install && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=... 3) npm run seed-index (creates a small local index) 4) npm run example (writes a trace to ./traces/session-YYYYMMDD.json) 5) python3 replay_harness.py ./traces/session-YYYYMMDD.json --assertions smoke_asserts.yaml 6) CI smoke job will run the same replay harness and surface diffs as artifacts.

Rollout plan: Merge to main guarded by reviewers + passing quickstarts-smoke CI job. Post-merge, add a small announcement in the quickstarts index and include a line in the next docs patch. The quickstart is intentionally lightweight so we can iterate on trace fields in follow-up PRs based on developer feedback.

Related work: This complements the RAG authoring studio and the existing telemetry probes work (ENG-4823). It is not a replacement for full fidelity tracing in production; instead, it is a developer-first reproducible trace format for quick root-cause analysis.

Open questions / future follow-ups: - Add a web-viewer UI for traces (low priority) - Extend the trace format to include sampling of model logits for deeper analysis (opt-in) - Add TypeScript smoke assertions generator for teams to encode domain-specific invariants.
commit_summary: scaffold: add quickstart directory with README and initial TS runner
feat: implement stepwise trace serializer and recorder hooks
ci: add quickstarts smoke workflow; fix lint and e2e flakes
review_thread: Diego Marquez (reviewer): Nice compact format — can we make the top_k default configurable via env var?
Anika Shah (author): Good call — added TOP_K env with default=5 in example-runner.ts
Priya Nair (reviewer): README needs a clearer section on PII redaction and the default mask. Also the replay harness should error non-zero if assertions fail.
Anika Shah (author): Updated README with redaction section and made the harness exit 1 on failed assertions (added tests).
Eliot Chen (reviewer): CI flaky network issue observed on e2e; suggest a retry wrapper or make network access optional. Approved after lint fixes.
Diego Marquez (approver): LGTM — merging once CI passes.
merge_outcome: merged into main via squash (merge commit message: 'Introduce stepwise RAG debug profiler quickstart — Anika Shah').
notes_for_maintainers: This quickstart intentionally uses a pinned lightweight model for CI; update the pinned model reference if underlying infra changes.
Follow-up PR should add a quick link in the quickstarts index page and a short entry in the docs site changelog.
